column3: The Hebrew joins her origin directly to her name without a separate “she was.”
The Hebrew explicitly says all his days and makes Jehoiada the active instructor; BSB uses passive instruction.
The Hebrew repeats the high places as the sacrifice location; BSB uses there.
The Hebrew retains assessed persons and what rises on a man’s heart; BSB specifies census money, vows, and voluntary gifts.
The Hebrew makes the priests the active repairers and names each man’s acquaintance; BSB has passive use for repair and a constituency.
The Hebrew explicitly calls Joash king; BSB says reign.
The Hebrew calls Jehoiada the priest without a separate other for the priests.
The Hebrew has two explicit negative purposes but no separate themselves.
The Hebrew explicitly numbers one chest.
The Hebrew gives tying before counting and has no explicit bags; BSB reverses the order and supplies bags.
The Hebrew calls the amount measured and repeats doing the work; BSB uses counted and supervised.
The Hebrew gives purchases and expenses as further objects without separate verbs for purchasing and paying.
The Hebrew makes the vessels the subjects of not being made; BSB makes money the subject of not being used.
The Hebrew has active plural giving agents; BSB uses passive payment.
The Hebrew retains their hand and active plural accounting agents; BSB uses passive required accounting.
The Hebrew repeats money with guilt and sins.
The Hebrew repeats Hazael and retains setting his face to go up; BSB uses he deciding to attack.
The Hebrew leaves the withdrawing king unnamed; BSB supplies Hazael.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the servants’ master unnamed, names Joash as the victim, and uses a striking verb; BSB names his servants and says killed.
Close to the Hebrew.
